generators.description: Whisper to a passerby. Tap to advance the cycle. Hire a Sycophant to auto-spread.

upgrades.name: Pre-Forum Whispers
upgrades.description: Sycophants speak earlier in the day.

upgrades.name: Senate Earshot
upgrades.description: Rumors travel further across the forum.

upgrades.name: Imperial Whisper Net
upgrades.description: Sycophants carry word across the provinces.

generators.factoid: Word-of-mouth rumor was the dominant information channel for most of human history. Plato's Phaedo and Xenophon both record political rumors moving through Athens within hours of events; the Roman writer Tacitus called rumor 'the unanimous voice of common ignorance.'

generators.description: Backdate your own legend in clay. Hire a Scribe to auto-forge.

upgrades.name: Better Clay
upgrades.description: Tablets bake harder, legends stick longer.

generators.factoid: The Mesopotamian 'naru' literary tradition fabricated royal inscriptions backdated by generations. Neo-Assyrian kings (722–612 BCE) commissioned naru texts in the name of Sargon of Akkad (~2334 BCE) to manufacture an ancestral political claim across 1,600 years of history.

generators.description: Leak a damning will. Hire a Pamphleteer for the relentless drumbeat.

upgrades.name: Triumvirate Backing
upgrades.description: A faction stands behind every smear.

generators.factoid: Octavian's 33–31 BCE propaganda war against Mark Antony included a 'will of Antony' allegedly bequeathing Roman provinces to Cleopatra. Most modern historians believe the document was forged by Octavian's staff; the Senate believed it, and declared war on Cleopatra rather than Antony.

generators.description: Pile-on litigation as harassment. The original troll.

upgrades.name: Bigger Dockets
upgrades.description: Sykophants file twice the suits each session.

generators.factoid: Athenian sykophants were professional accusers who profited from successful prosecutions, creating direct financial incentives to fabricate charges. The system became so corrupt that 5th-century BCE laws penalised sykophants whose cases fell below a 20% conviction rate.

generators.description: Stamp your image into every transaction. Era's flagship.

upgrades.name: Provincial Mints
upgrades.description: Branches mint from Hispania to Syria.

upgrades.name: Divi Filius Stamp
upgrades.description: Every coin proclaims your divine descent.

generators.factoid: Augustus' systematic image-control over Roman coinage put his face into every household in the empire — the first mass-distributed political portrait in history. Successor emperors continued the practice; coins of disgraced rulers were melted and reissued under damnatio memoriae.

prestige_bridge_copy: The tablets crumble. The temples weather. The playbook does not. A new technology arrives — the press — and with it, the same human appetite for the convenient lie.
